summary:
Tokat province has no trans-specific statute, enforcement record or documented incident of its own in the sources for this record. The only region-specific signal is that provincial authorities and police in Tokat operate within the nationwide pattern in which visible LGBT assembly is routinely banned and policed, so any visible LGBT gathering in the province would be policed on that basis rather than under any Tokat-specific measure.

Tokat stands under Turkey's national framework. The visitor-facing assessment of Turkish law, policing practice, detention conditions, document rules and protection machinery is carried by the national record and is not reproduced here.
tangentialFactors: No Tokat-specific adjacent factors were identified. The sources document no provincial ordinance, police directive, governor's order or provincial human-rights body bearing on trans visitors in Tokat, and no local incident involving a trans person in the province.
localsOnly: No Tokat-specific resident-facing facts appear in the sources: nothing on provincial services, local healthcare access, local administrative practice or local enforcement against trans residents. The legal position of trans residents of Tokat is set by the national framework, which the national record covers.
outOfScopeNotes: Tokat is addressed in the sources only by inference from the nationwide pattern of assembly bans, not by documented provincial enforcement. No count of detentions, prosecutions, prosecutorial referrals or violent incidents in Tokat was located, and no provincial authority was found to have issued a statement on trans or LGBT matters. Whether the province has applied the assembly-ban pattern in any specific year is unresolved in the sources.
